title: QTestBench: A Test Framework for Evaluating LLM-Generated Quantum Code

body: Large language models (LLMs) have shown strong results in classical code generation and are increasingly used to write the unit tests that safeguard that code. Whether they can do the same for quantum software is less clear, because quantum programs are probabilistic, depend on numerical tolerances, and are judged by domain-specific checkers, so a well-formed test can still disagree with the benchmark's verdict. Existing quantum benchmarks measure whether a model produces a correct solution, but not whether its tests can distinguish correct implementations from faulty ones. We introduce QTestBench, a framework that evaluates LLM-generated quantum test suites against independent benchmark checkers, never treating the tests themselves as ground truth. For each task, QTestBench prompts models to produce syntactic, semantic, and behavioral tests, injects candidate solutions at runtime, and compares each test verdict with the checker's label under three validation cohorts, each answering a distinct diagnostic question. We benchmark five LLMs on eight PennyLane QHack challenges and ten Qiskit HumanEval tasks. Generated suites almost always execute, but discrimination lags behind: the best generator reaches a test quality of 0.71 on QHack and 0.34 on Qiskit HumanEval, so executability alone overstates test quality. Oracle-verified synthetic mutants stabilize bug-detection estimates when natural faulty solutions are scarce, as on three of ten Qiskit tasks that yield none. QTestBench offers a reproducible, cross-framework benchmark for the trustworthiness of LLM-generated quantum tests.
summaryZh: 为了填补量子软件领域缺乏对大模型生成测试套件鉴别能力评估的空白，本文引入了QTestBench框架。该框架不将模型生成的测试本身视为真理，而是将其与独立的基准检查器进行对比验证。测试五个大模型在PennyLane和Qiskit任务上的表现发现，尽管模型生成的测试绝大多数能够执行，但其对正确与错误实现的区分能力仍有待提升。该框架为量子代码生成的可信度提供了可复现的评测手段。
